results.primary_cause: Evidence is conflicting: 2026 dry-bulk rates and Capesize demand were reported as strong, but BIMCO warned that the strength was partly rerouting-driven and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut; durability and breadth of the exact freight cycle remain unresolved.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk freight-rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial and caused by forced rerouting, with the boost expected to reverse and supply potentially producing a 2027 glut.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse

results.primary_cause: Available evidence indicates ongoing storage and NAND-related demand, but it does not establish a sufficiently time-consistent exact NAND pricing, controller/module, inventory, or utilization cycle; counter-search results were also broadly supportive rather than contradictory.

supporting_evidence.claim: The 2026 Future of Memory and Storage Conference highlighted continued growth in storage and memory markets and increasing AI-driven storage demand.
supporting_evidence.source_title: 2026 FMS Shows Storage And Memory Market Continued Growth

counter_evidence.claim: A NAND-controller company executive described structural changes in storage demand and argued that supply may not respond to demand in the historical manner, which does not provide evidence of a broad cyclical reversal.
counter_evidence.source_title: The Next NAND Decade: Why Supply Can’t Catch Demand The Way It Used To
